Rainfall in Lebanon

Lebanon has a Mediterranean climate with wet winters and dry summers. Most of the rain falls between November and March, and the mountains receive much more rain and snow than the coast.

Beirut gets about 825 millimetres of rain in a normal year, while the Bekaa valley, sheltered by the Mount Lebanon range, is much drier. Zahle receives roughly 600 millimetres and Baalbek even less.

The wettest month in Beirut is usually January. Summer months from June to September are almost completely dry, with clear skies and high humidity on the coast.

Snow covers the high peaks for several months, and melting snow feeds the Litani and Orontes rivers through spring and early summer.
